newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Transnet has been covertly negotiating the sale of its loss-making cellular phone division to cellular provider MTN, with a deal set for completion next month - barely a year after Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau blocked a similar move.

- Government has approved the sale of its leisure company Aventura, with at least ten local bidders -- mostly consortiums with a black empowerment element -- expressing strong interest in the parastatal.

- Anglo American Corporation of SA Ltd and Worldwide Africa Investments had entered into discussions for Worldwide to take a strategic stake in Anglo-controlled assurer Southern Life Association Ltd, high level sources confirmed.

- Government back-pedalled on Tuesday from the propsed three billion rand sale of defence equipment to Syria, saying any tender for the sale would be issued after 1999 and a final decision need only be made then.
- South Africa is to reject the terms of a trade agreement proposed by the EU, and will challenge its entire approach to the economic development of southern African states.

- Only about 1,000 tax dodgers have sent in applications for amnesty since the November start of the government's latest and avowedly last tax amnesty scheme, figures released on Tuesday by the South African Revenue Service showed.

- South Africa's two largest unions, the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) and the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (Numsa), ended their two week-long boycott of talks on Tuesday on the restructuring of Eskom.

- Virgin Atlantic Airways, which is pursuing a 35 percent stake in the state-owned domestic airline Sun Air, would settle for ten percent less should the government stick to its decision to sell no more than 25 percent to a foreign shareholder, Davis James, Virgin's general manager for southern Africa, said on Tuesday.

- Newshelf 71, a consortium led by New Africa Investments, is seeking permission to appeal against last month's Pretoria Supreme Court ruling which overturned the Independent Broadcasting Authority's (IBA) decision to grant the consortium the private broadcasting licence for Radio Jacaranda.
- No permit to sell arms has been granted to South African companies to export military equipment to Syria, the Department of Foreign Affiars said on Tuesday.
